fieldMarks: Females 273-292 mm carapace and up to about 1.9 kg; males 113-127 mm.
Relatively low-domed shell with a black median keel and pale yellow outline; concentric yellow semicircles on each marginal scute.
Head with a large light interorbital blotch connected to postorbital blotches; no nasal trident.
Females have larger heads, broader jaws and elongated front claws; males longer, thicker tails.
behavior: Diurnal and active roughly March-November; bask on logs with limbs and neck stretched out.
Turtles feed or bask on logs May-October; daily torpor begins below about 19 C before hibernation.
Mainly molluscivorous; males and juveniles eat smaller bivalves and aquatic insects.
habitat: Medium-sized rivers to large creeks with sand bars, sandy banks, logs, deep pools and abundant mollusks; nests in sand bars and banks.
range: Mobile Bay drainage: eastern Mississippi, throughout Alabama and northwestern Georgia. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Pascagoula map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Higher-domed shell with spines on the keel; nasal trident usually present.
